heading: Multi-source BFS unlocks shortest paths
body:
**Start from ALL 0s at once** — not one cell at a time.

BFS explores level-by-level in distance order, so the **first time** it reaches any cell = shortest distance to *any* 0.

No need to try every 0 individually!

heading: Mark unvisited cells with -1
body:
Initialize output grid to `-1` (unknown distance).

During BFS, when you hit a neighbor with `-1` → it's **unvisited** — update it and enqueue.

This avoids revisiting cells and keeps BFS efficient.

label: Crux · Python

q: Why do we enqueue all 0 cells at the start instead of processing each cell individually?
options: It reduces memory usage by avoiding duplicate queue entries
Multi-source BFS guarantees the first visit to any cell is the shortest path from any 0
It allows us to process the matrix in parallel on multiple cores
It makes the code simpler by avoiding nested loops
explain: Multi-source BFS explores all sources simultaneously in distance order. The first time any cell is reached, it must be via the shortest path from some 0.
